name: verification-run-ergonomics-and-seatbelt
title: Add a verification_run command, make the stale-evidence refresh re-execute the pinned command, and add a fail-open PreToolUse early-warning hook
description:
Follow-on to the tool-executed evidence-receipts enforcement floor (story B-ec67). That story made verification_evidence_add / verification_evidence_batch_add execute a pinned (command,selector) and stamp a receipt, and demote a stale-refreshed receipt to non-mechanical. This story adds the ergonomics + early-warning layers so the correct action is the path of least resistance.

Three deliverables:
1. verification_run command: `lattice verification_run --storyId --intentRef` resolves the intent, executes its pinned verifier, captures exit/output, and atomically writes the receipt — so a caller never authors a pass command by hand. Ideally verification_evidence_add stops accepting a caller-authored command for automated proof at all and instead consumes an internally-generated receipt id.
2. Stale-evidence refresh RE-EXECUTES the pinned command: today the stale-evidence refresh only demotes a receipt (from the enforcement-floor story) so it can no longer launder; this story makes it re-run the pinned command and re-issue a real receipt when the material changed, closing the loop (the interim per-row laundering guard is story B-3b88; the receipt shape is B-ec67).
3. PreToolUse fail-open early-warning hook: mirror the existing scope-guard hook (.claude/hooks/lattice-scope-pretool.cjs + handlers/prewrite-guard.ts + its smoke) — a thin host shim that spawns a read-only CLI verdict command and denies early with a teaching message when a caller tries to record evidence whose command/selector does not match the pinned intent, BEFORE the write runs. Fail-open (the handler is the real floor); both hosts; gate the Codex side on an e2e test that uses Codex's real emitted shell-tool name.

This is the ergonomics + seatbelt layer; the enforcement floor and the write-time refusals already shipped in B-ec67.
